title: $62,000 a Year Is How Much an Hour? (2026)
metaDescription: $62,000 a year is $29.81/hour at 40 hrs/week — $1,192.31 weekly, $5,167 monthly. Full 2026 breakdown with a federal take-home estimate.

hero.lede: Based on a 40-hour week worked 52 weeks a year (2,080 hours). Below: every pay-period equivalent, the rate at other workweeks, a 2026 federal take-home estimate, and how $62,000 compares with the U.S. median.

shortAnswer.heading: How much is $62,000 a year per hour?
shortAnswer.html: $62,000 a year is $29.81 an hour at 40 hours a week, 52 weeks a year (2,080 hours). That's $238.46 a day, $1,192.31 a week, $2,384.62 biweekly, and $5,166.67 a month — all gross. After estimated federal income tax and FICA, a single filer keeps about $51,997 a year, roughly $4,333 a month.

sections.title: What $62,000 looks like per paycheck.
sections.note: All figures are gross (pre-tax). See the take-home table below for the federal-only estimate after taxes.

sections.title: Where $62,000 stands in 2026.
paragraphs: At 40 hours a week, $62,000 a year is $29.81 an hour. That is the offer-letter number, not the bank-deposit number: gross pay lands at $2,384.62 per biweekly check, and what actually arrives depends on taxes and benefits withheld.

That lands almost exactly on the U.S. median: the Bureau of Labor Statistics puts median weekly earnings for full-time workers at $1,251 (BLS, Q2 2026), which annualizes to about $65,052. A useful rule of thumb at this level: every extra $1 of hourly pay is worth about $2,080 a year at full time, so small raises compound faster than they feel.

sections.title: The hourly rate depends on your hours.
sections.note: Salaried roles rarely pay overtime — at 45 hours a week the same $62,000 effectively pays $26.50 per hour worked.

sections.title: From $62,000 gross to take-home.
sections.note: Single filer, standard deduction, no state/local income tax, no credits or pre-tax benefits. Your actual paycheck will differ.

sections.title: Why the 12% bracket doesn't mean 12% tax.
paragraphs: Only $45,900 of this salary is actually taxable federally once the 2026 standard deduction of $16,100 is applied. Federal income tax totals $5,260 — a 8.5% effective rate even though the marginal bracket is 12% — and employee FICA adds $4,743.

After those federal deductions, take-home is roughly $51,997 a year — $1,999.88 per biweekly paycheck. On a 50/30/20 plan that budget supports about $2,167/month of essentials, $1,300/month of discretionary spending, and $867/month toward savings, before any state income tax.

faq.q: How much is $62,000 a year per hour?
faq.a: $62,000 a year is $29.81 an hour at 40 hours a week (2,080 hours a year). At 37.5 hours a week it rises to $31.79 an hour, and if you actually work 45-hour weeks it averages $26.50 per hour worked.

faq.q: How much is $62,000 a year biweekly?
faq.a: Gross biweekly pay on $62,000 is $2,384.62 ($62,000 ÷ 26 pay periods). After estimated federal income tax and FICA for a single filer, roughly $1,999.88 per check remains — before state taxes and benefits.

faq.q: How much is $62,000 a year after taxes?
faq.a: Using 2026 federal brackets and the $16,100 standard deduction, a single filer earning $62,000 pays about $5,260 in federal income tax and $4,743 in FICA, keeping roughly $51,997 a year ($4,333.08 a month). This is a federal-only estimate — state and local taxes reduce it further.

$62,000 is right around the U.S. median full-time salary of about $65,052 (BLS, Q2 2026: $1,251/week). Whether it is "good" depends heavily on your metro's cost of living, household size, and debt load — the same salary goes much further in a low-cost region than in an expensive coastal city.

faq.q: What tax bracket is $62,000 in for 2026?
faq.a: After the $16,100 standard deduction, $62,000 leaves $45,900 of taxable income, which puts a single filer in the 12% marginal bracket for 2026. Only income above each threshold is taxed at the higher rate, so the effective federal rate is just 8.5%.

methodology: Conversions are straight arithmetic on gross salary: $62,000 ÷ 2,080 hours (40 × 52) for hourly, ÷ 260 workdays for daily, ÷ 52, 26, 24 and 12 for the pay-period figures. No taxes are applied to those rows.

The take-home estimate uses 2026 federal brackets for a single filer with the $16,100 standard deduction, plus employee FICA (6.2% Social Security + 1.45% Medicare). It excludes state/local income tax, credits, and pre-tax benefits such as 401(k) or health premiums — so real paychecks will differ.
The median comparison uses BLS median usual weekly earnings for full-time wage and salary workers: $1,251/week (BLS, Q2 2026).
Educational estimates only — not tax, legal, or financial advice.
